messages.subject_clean: Is there a way to get the sense and anti-sense annotation for each read in the featureCounts output bam file
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jerry,

This information can be retrieved from the FLAG field (bit 0x10) of each read included in the bam file. featureCounts does not change the existing fields of the provided bam file. It just adds assignment result to each read in the bam file.

Regards,

Wei

messages.subject: featureCounts: counting paired end fragment insert regions
messages.subject_clean: featureCounts: counting paired end fragment insert regions
messages.body_plain:
I was trying to apply featureCounts in a bit of a non-canonical way, and ended up with a behavior I wasn't expecting. I'll provide more context below, but my general question is whether it is intended behavior for paired end reads to not count towards features that exist solely within the insert region of the paired reads.

I've attached a image demonstrating this, although I'll need to explain what I've done here first. I've been testing various tools to look for an accurate method of calculating paired-end fragment coverage (in E. coli; as a sidenote, I'll welcome suggestions for any such tools to try, particularly if they do not impose arbitrary requirements for the 'properly-paired' flag to be set). I'm sure this wasn't your intended purpose for featureCounts, but I tried this out with an annotation file that essentially defines 1 feature per base over the entire genome, then quantitated reads allowing for multi-overlap.

I ran this in both the R and standalone versions, with the same results:
In R (Rsubread_1.30.6):
featureCounts(files=file, annot.ext=anno, nthreads=3, allowMultiOverlap = T, isPairedEnd = T, strandSpecific = 0)

In OSX Terminal (featureCounts v1.6.2):
featureCounts -a anno.saf -F SAF -p -O -o FCcounts  data.bam

I then turned the resulting counts into a bigwig file and loaded it into IGV (the blue data_both.bw <http://data_both.bw> track; 'both' as in unstranded counting). For the purposes of demonstration, I extracted just a small window of reads using IGV (attached bam file) and performed this analysis on only those reads, as shown in the attached screenshot. I set IGV to display reads as pairs; in this mode, the insert region between two reads is indicated by the thin grey line connecting the red and blue reads.

What you can see is that, although featureCount does avoid double-counting overlapped forward/reverse reads of the same fragment, the insert region of the fragment in the third row is not counted in the coverage file (the depth is 2, compared to just upstream where the depth is 3). I don't know if this is an edge case that specifically arises from these small feature sizes, or if this is in general the intended behavior towards insert regions. I'd. have thought that analyzing paired reads would count coverage the same way over the entire fragment, but this doesn't necessarily seem to be true.

Also, as a sidenote, I did look into the coverageCount tool. This behaved as expected when counting as unpaired reads, however, when counting reads as paired I don't really understand what is going on. For instance, the depth at 2,320,560 is "2", at 2,320,600 is "2", and at 2,320,680 is "4"... none of those make sense, plus everything is in multiples of 2 (literally only 0, 2,4, or 6). I'd wonder if I was reading the file incorrectly, except the unpaired coverageCount output seems reasonable (eg, at 2,320,560 it is "3", at 2,320,600 is "3",  and at 2,320,680 is "4").

I used in R:
file <- "covCount_p-NC_000913.bin"
x <- readBin(file, integer(), size=4, endian="little", n=file.info(file)$size/4)
pos <- 2320600
left <- pos-80
right <- pos+120
cov <- data.frame(pos=left:right, cov=x[left:right])

In any case, I would appreciate any guidance towards either of these issues. Thanks very much

messages.subject: Re: featureCounts: counting paired end fragment insert regions
messages.subject_clean: featureCounts: counting paired end fragment insert regions
messages.body_plain:
Yes this is the intended behavior of featureCounts. When counting read pairs, it requires at least one read base overlapping the feature. The gap between the two reads from the same pair is not considered. Note that the size of this gap could be very big when the two reads are mapped to different exons and this gap could include both insert sequence and intron sequence, therefore we do not consider the gap when counting read pairs.

Regarding coverageCount, this seems to be a bug. We will investigate it.

messages.subject: STAR output to featureCount-resorting
messages.body_plain:
Hi Subread team,

 I really like this awesome tool, especially the fast performance of featureCount. I recently need to process a lot of samples using STAR aligner, then count read by featureCount. But the problem I got is: no matter I set "--outSAMtype BAM Unsorted" or "--outSAMtype BAM SortedByCoordinate" in STAR, featureCount always re-sort the bam. I read this thread <http://seqanswers.com/forums/showthread.php?t=49687> about the incompatibility of STAR/samtools sort. Just wondering if there are any changes in the new version? I guess I can use "−−donotsort " on STAR sorted bam files? How is the accuracy?

 Many thanks!

Ji
